summary: The shape of content that has not arrived yet.
note: No Figma component exists for Skeleton. Built from the system's own tokens; worth drawing in Figma before it spreads.

pairs.dont: Show three generic grey bars where a table will land.
pairs.do: Match the shape and count of what is actually coming.
pairs.why: A skeleton is a promise about the layout. Break it and the page jumps, which is worse than having shown nothing.

pairs.dont: Let a screen reader meet twelve skeleton blocks.
pairs.do: Hide them (they already are) and announce the wait once on the region.
pairs.why: Twelve empty boxes read out one at a time tells the person nothing about what is happening.

pairs.dont: Flash skeletons for a request that usually takes 200ms.
pairs.do: Show them only past about half a second, or keep the old content in place.
pairs.why: A skeleton that appears and vanishes reads as a glitch. Below the threshold, nothing at all is calmer.

pairs.dont: Use a skeleton for a submit, a save, or an action in flight.
pairs.do: Use the button's loading state; save skeletons for content arriving.
pairs.why: A skeleton says "this will be here shortly". An action has no shape to stand in for.

pairs.dont: Skeleton the nav, the page title and the buttons too.
pairs.do: Render the frame for real and skeleton only what is loading.
pairs.why: Chrome is already known at render time. Greying it out makes the whole page look broken rather than busy.
